question: Which festival traces its origin to the Tibetan New Year and in Ladakh, it is celebrated every year at the end of the harvesting season?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Losar festival.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Losar festival:-**

 
 
• It​ is a **Tibetan festival** that marks the **Tibetan New Year **and is celebrated in **Ladakh** at the end of the **harvesting season.**
 
• It is a **three-day festival **that is celebrated with great enthusiasm by the **Tibetan and Ladakhi communities.**
 
• The festival is marked by various** rituals**, including the **burning of incense, offerings to the deities**, and **traditional dance performances.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Matho Nagrang:-**

 
 
• It​** **is a festival celebrated in the **Matho Monastery of Ladakh**, and it involves the performance of **masked dances.**
 
 
 
• **Yuru Kabgyat:-**
 
 
• It is another festival celebrated in **Ladakh**, which involves the worship of the** Buddhist deity Vajrakilaya** and the performance of traditional dances.
 
 
 
• **Dosmoche:-**
 
 
• It​** **is a festival celebrated in **Leh, Ladakh**, to mark the **end of winter **and the beginning of the **sowing season**.
 
• It involves the performance of **masked dances** and the** burning of effigies.**
